Several studies have found that the factor that has a significant effect on the number of maternal postpartum mortality is the percentage of pregnant women who had a pregnancy visit K4 [16]. Furthermore, there is research on the number of maternal postpartum mortality, with one of the factors affecting maternal mortality is the percentage of handling obstetric complications in each district/city [17]. Another study on the number of maternal postpartum mortality found that one of the factors affecting maternal postpartum mortality was the percentage of pregnant women who had a pregnancy visit K1 [18]. There is also research on factors that are thought to affect maternal mortality such as the percentage of households receiving cash assistance and the ratio of health centers and hospitals [19].

steps.title: Collect Data and Coordinates
steps.instruction: Gather case data on the number of maternal postpartum mortality in East Java Province for 2020, including the longitude and latitude coordinates for each district.

steps.title: Perform Multicollinearity Test
steps.instruction: Detect multicollinearity among predictor variables using the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF).

substeps.instruction: Calculate VIF for each predictor variable.
Verify that VIF values are less than 10 to ensure no multicollinearity exists.

steps.title: Test Distribution Suitability
steps.instruction: Determine if the data follows a Poisson distribution using the Kolmogorov Smirnov Test.

substeps.instruction: Set hypotheses: H0 (Data follows Poisson distribution) and H1 (Data does not follow Poisson distribution).
Use a significance level of α = 0.05.
Calculate the test statistic D = max|F(x) - S(x)|.

steps.title: Analyze Global Poisson Regression
steps.instruction: Estimate parameters for a standard Poisson regression model to establish a baseline.

substeps.instruction: Use the Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) method with Newton-Raphson iterations to estimate parameters.
Perform simultaneous and partial significance testing of the parameters.
Calculate the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Deviance.

steps.title: Analyze Generalized Poisson Regression (GPR)
steps.instruction: Apply GPR to address overdispersion or underdispersion if the Poisson model's Deviance divided by degrees of freedom is significantly different from 1.

substeps.instruction: Estimate parameters (ϕ, β0, β1...βk) using MLE with Newton-Raphson iterations.
Alternatively, estimate ϕ using the method of moments by equating the Pearson Chi-Square statistic with the degrees of freedom.
Perform simultaneous and partial significance testing.
Calculate the AIC value.

steps.title: Test for Spatial Heterogeneity
steps.instruction: Determine if predictor variables have unequal effects across different locations using the Breusch-Pagan (BP) test.

substeps.instruction: Set hypotheses: H0 (Variance between locations is equal) and H1 (Variance between locations is different).
Calculate the BP statistic: BP = 1/2 fT Z(ZT Z)^-1 ZT f.
Reject H0 if BP > X(α, k)^2 or p-value < α.

steps.title: Determine Optimum Bandwidth
steps.instruction: Find the best bandwidth (h) for spatial weighting using the Cross-Validation (CV) method.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the Euclidean distance between observation locations based on geographical position.
Evaluate three kernel functions: Fixed Bisquare, Fixed Tricube, and Adaptive Bisquare.
Select the kernel function and bandwidth value that produces the minimum CV value.

steps.title: Estimate GWGPR Model Parameters
steps.instruction: Perform Geographically Weighted Generalized Poisson Regression (GWGPR) to produce local parameter estimators for each location.

substeps.instruction: Determine (ui, vi) coordinates for each district.
Initialize estimated parameters β^(ui, vi)(0).
Form the gradient vector (g) and the Hessian matrix (H) based on the log-likelihood function.
Iterate using the formula: β^(ui, vi)(m+1) = β^(ui, vi)(m) − H^-1(β^(ui, vi)(m)) g(β^(ui, vi)(m)).
Stop iteration when |β^(ui, vi)(m+1) − β^(ui, vi)(m)| ≤ ε.

steps.title: Test GWGPR Parameter Significance
steps.instruction: Evaluate the significance of the local parameters for the GWGPR model.

substeps.instruction: Perform a simultaneous Maximum Likelihood Ratio Test (MLRT) using the deviance value D(β^).
Perform partial parameter testing for each variable p at each location using the statistic Z = β^p(ui, vi) / se(β^p(ui, vi)).
Reject H0 if |Z| > Z(α/2) (e.g., 1.96 for α = 0.05).

steps.title: Select the Best Model
steps.instruction: Compare the Poisson, GPR, and GWGPR models to determine the most accurate representation of the data.

substeps.instruction: Compare the AIC values of all three models.
Select the model with the smallest AIC value as the best model.
